name: Delegation Graph
what_it_shows: The live spawn topology of how a parent session delegates work to agent-* subagents.
notes: Genuinely novel; no other tool shows your agent's delegation topology. Nodes sized by event_count, edges = parent->child spawn. Sovereignty story: see who acted on your behalf. [built] resolution works reliably (~12-14 children per parent via tool_result agentId echoes, phantom-filtered); the view samples the top-10 delegators so shows a subset — resolving all 631 needs sampling all parents or a server-side parent index.
hypothesis: Parent sessions fan out to multiple subagents in recognizable delegation shapes (wide fan-outs, deep chains) that expose how work is decomposed.
falsifier: If almost every session_id starting with 'agent-' has no resolvable parent (flat, orphaned subagents), the graph degenerates into disconnected dots and reveals no topology.
witness: GET /api/sessions → count session_id LIKE 'agent-%' vs those that resolve to a parent session; needs a substantial share (>~30%) with a linkable parent, else no edges to draw.

name: Delegation Dendrogram
what_it_shows: A tidy top-down tree of parent sessions and their subagent lineage.
notes: Cheaper, deterministic alternative to the force graph; better for reading exact lineage. d3-hierarchy tree, no physics.
hypothesis: Delegation is genuinely hierarchical (a rooted tree with depth >1), so a dendrogram reads lineage more clearly than a physics graph.
falsifier: If max delegation depth is 1 (parents spawn leaves but subagents never spawn their own), the tree collapses to a two-level star and a simple list would do.
witness: GET /api/sessions → derive parent links and compute max tree depth; needs depth ≥ 2 for a dendrogram to beat a flat list.

name: Agent x Project Adjacency Matrix
what_it_shows: Where each agent does its work: a colored grid of session/event volume per agent-project cell.
notes: Cross-tab already exists in analytics; just needs a rect grid. Sortable rows/cols reveal clusters (Cuthill-McKee optional).
hypothesis: Agents specialize across projects, so the (agent x project) grid shows an uneven, block-structured fill rather than uniform coverage.
falsifier: If there is effectively one agent, or every agent touches every project evenly, the matrix is a single row or a flat block and carries no signal.
witness: GET /api/sessions → count distinct origin_agent and distinct project_id; needs ≥2 agents and ≥3 projects with an uneven cell distribution to be informative.

name: Session Duration Beeswarm by Agent
what_it_shows: The full distribution of session durations, one dot per session, grouped by agent.
notes: Shows spread and outliers Scatter hides. forceX + collide dodge. Click dot -> Story.
hypothesis: Session durations are broadly spread with agent-specific modes and long-tail outliers that a beeswarm surfaces per agent.
falsifier: If duration is missing/near-constant for most rows, or one agent dominates all points, the swarm is a single tight clump with nothing to compare.
witness: GET /api/sessions → derive duration = last_event - start_time; needs a spread of ≥2 decades and ≥2 agents with enough sessions each to form distinct swarms.

name: Events-over-Time Streamgraph by Agent
what_it_shows: How activity volume ebbs and flows across days, stacked and colored by agent.
notes: stack.offset(wiggle). Reads the rhythm of work; complements the calendar heatmap with a flow view.
hypothesis: Event volume varies across days with shifting agent composition, producing a flowing stacked band that reveals work rhythm.
falsifier: If activity spans too few days, or a single agent supplies ~all events, the streamgraph is one flat lump indistinguishable from a bar.
witness: GET /api/sessions → bucket start_time by day; needs ≥ ~7 active days and ≥2 agents contributing meaningfully per day.

name: Agent <-> Project Chord
what_it_shows: Ribbons connecting agents to the projects they touch, weighted by activity.
notes: Pretty and legible for few agents/projects; degrades past ~20 nodes. d3-chord + ribbon.
hypothesis: Agents and projects form a many-to-many web where several agents share projects, giving the chord meaningful cross-links.
falsifier: If agent<->project is near-diagonal (each agent maps to one project), the chord shows only trivial self-links and reveals nothing.
witness: GET /api/sessions → count distinct (origin_agent, project_id) pairs with >1 session; needs ≥ ~8 cross-pairs to justify a chord over a matrix.

name: Token Distribution Ridgeline per Agent
what_it_shows: Overlapping density curves of output-token counts, one ridge per agent.
notes: Log-binned KDE over 6 decades. Reveals whether an agent is chatty or terse. area + curveBasis.
hypothesis: Different agents have distinguishable token-output distributions (some terse, some verbose) that stacked density ridges make comparable.
falsifier: If per-agent token distributions overlap almost completely, or only one agent has enough sessions, the ridges coincide and add nothing over one histogram.
witness: GET /api/sessions → group total_output_tokens by origin_agent; needs ≥2 agents each with ≥ ~30 sessions and visibly different medians.

name: Session->Subagent Arc Diagram
what_it_shows: Sessions on a time-ordered baseline with arcs linking parents to spawned subagents.
notes: 1D layout keeps chronology; arc height encodes spawn distance in time. Good for a dense single-day view.
hypothesis: Parent and subagent sessions are close in time, so arcs over a chronological baseline reveal bursts of delegation.
falsifier: If parent->subagent links cannot be resolved (same orphan problem as the graph), there are no arcs to draw.
witness: GET /api/sessions?limit=all → count resolvable parent->child links within a single day window; needs ≥ ~5 links in a day to be worth the layout.

name: Session Parallel Coordinates
what_it_shows: Each session as a polyline across events / tokens / duration / turns to spot multivariate outliers.
notes: Brushable axes = filter. Reveals e.g. 'many events, few tokens' sessions. Color by agent.
hypothesis: The four axes are not perfectly correlated, so polylines cross and reveal off-diagonal sessions (e.g. high events, low tokens).
falsifier: If events/tokens/duration are near-perfectly correlated, every line is parallel and the plot degenerates into one thick band.
witness: GET /api/sessions → compute pairwise correlation among event_count, total_output_tokens, duration; needs at least one pair with |r| < ~0.8 to show crossings.

name: Project Activity Bump Chart
what_it_shows: How projects rise and fall in activity rank week over week.
notes: line + curveBumpX over per-week rank. Narrative of where attention shifts over time.
hypothesis: Project attention shifts over weeks, so their activity ranks cross and produce a readable bump narrative.
falsifier: If one project dominates every week (rank never changes) or history spans <2 weeks, the lines are flat and parallel.
witness: GET /api/sessions → rank projects by weekly event volume; needs ≥3 weeks and ≥2 projects that actually swap ranks.

name: Calendar Ribbon
what_it_shows: A continuous day-by-day ribbon of session intensity, distinct from the discrete contribution grid.
notes: Overlaps conceptually with existing heatmap; lower marginal value. Kept for completeness.
hypothesis: A continuous ribbon reads day-over-day momentum better than the discrete contribution grid.
falsifier: If it merely restates the existing heatmap's daily counts with no added temporal reading, it is redundant by construction.
witness: Compare against existing heatmap: if daily aggregate == heatmap cell values with no new derived signal, reject as duplicate.

name: Tool->Tool Transition Chord
what_it_shows: Cyclic tool-usage grammar (e.g. Edit->Bash->Read loops) that a bipartite sankey cannot show.
notes: Flow mode is bipartite (source|target); chord captures self-loops and cycles the sankey flattens.
hypothesis: Tool usage forms cycles (Edit->Bash->Read->Edit) that the existing bipartite Flow sankey cannot represent but a chord can.
falsifier: If the tool transition matrix is effectively acyclic/feed-forward, the chord adds nothing the sankey did not already show.
witness: Aggregate tool->tool transitions from event records (via /api/sessions/{id}/records or analytics); needs measurable back-edges/self-loops for a chord to beat Flow.

name: Tool Transition Adjacency Heatmap
what_it_shows: A from x to grid of tool-transition frequencies, readable at a glance for hot pairs.
notes: Cheapest high-value item: reuse Flow's transition counts, render as rects. Diagonal = tool repetition.
hypothesis: A few tool pairs dominate transitions, producing bright hot cells that make the agent's habitual grammar legible.
falsifier: If transitions are near-uniform across all tool pairs, the grid is flat and no pattern stands out.
witness: Reuse the transition counts Flow already computes; needs a skewed distribution (top few pairs >> the rest) to show hot cells.

name: Turn-Phase Icicle
data_shape: turn phases / eval-apply within a session
what_it_shows: A single session decomposed into turns -> phases -> tool calls as nested horizontal bars.
notes: Linear cousin of Sunburst but per-session and phase-aware; complements Story's linear scroll.
hypothesis: A session decomposes into multi-level turn->phase->tool structure worth showing as nested bars.
falsifier: If sessions have essentially one turn or no phase detection, the icicle is a single flat bar with no hierarchy.
witness: GET /api/sessions/{id}/records for a busy session → count distinct turns and phases; needs ≥3 turns with detectable phase structure.

name: User x Project Marimekko
what_it_shows: Proportional mosaic of who works on what, column width = user share, segment height = project share.
notes: Good for team/fleet story; encodes two proportions at once. Rect math only.
hypothesis: Multiple users split their effort across projects unevenly, so a mosaic conveys both user share and per-user project mix.
falsifier: If there is effectively one user, the mosaic collapses to a single column and the two-proportion encoding is wasted.
witness: GET /api/sessions → count distinct user values with >1 session; needs ≥2 active users for the marimekko to mean anything.

name: Fleet Topology Graph
what_it_shows: Your fleet as a graph: principals -> hosts -> agents -> active sessions.
notes: Directly serves the personhood/fleet story; multi-level force layout. Higher build cost due to level constraints.
hypothesis: The fleet spans multiple principals/hosts/agents forming a multi-level graph that makes 'who and what is in my fleet' visible at a glance.
falsifier: If there is one principal on one host with one agent, the graph is a trivial star and tells the user nothing they don't know.
witness: GET /api/sessions → count distinct principal_id, host, origin_agent; needs ≥2 in at least two of those dimensions to form real topology.

name: Agent Swimlane Timeline
what_it_shows: Sessions laid on time, one swimlane per agent, to see concurrency across agents.
notes: Existing Gantt packs by group generically; this is a fixed agent-lane variant. Marginal over current Gantt.
hypothesis: Agents run concurrently in overlapping time windows, which fixed per-agent lanes make obvious.
falsifier: If sessions rarely overlap in time or there is one agent, the swimlanes show no concurrency and the generic Gantt already suffices.
witness: GET /api/sessions → check for overlapping [start_time,last_event] intervals across ≥2 agents; needs measurable overlap to justify a dedicated view.

name: Events x Tokens Hexbin Density
what_it_shows: Density of sessions in the events-vs-tokens plane where the Scatter view overplots.
notes: d3-hexbin plugin. Directly upgrades Scatter for 800+ points where dots collide. Log axes.
hypothesis: With 800+ sessions the events-vs-tokens Scatter overplots, and hexbin density reveals concentration Scatter hides.
falsifier: If total session count is small (<~200) or points are well separated, Scatter already reads fine and binning adds nothing.
witness: GET /api/sessions → total count and overplot check in the events/tokens plane; needs ≥ ~500 points with visible clumping to warrant hexbin.

name: Session Fingerprint Radar
what_it_shows: A single session's shape across normalized axes (events, tokens-in, tokens-out, duration, tools, errors).
notes: Good compact 'what kind of session was this' glyph; overlay two for comparison. lineRadial.
hypothesis: Sessions have distinguishable multi-axis fingerprints, so overlaying two radars makes their character comparable at a glance.
falsifier: If the chosen axes are highly correlated, every radar is the same near-regular polygon and comparison is uninformative.
witness: GET /api/sessions → sample 2-3 sessions and normalize the axes; needs visibly different axis profiles between sessions to be worth a glyph.

name: Lineage Circle-Pack
what_it_shows: Parent sessions as circles containing their subagent circles, sized by event volume.
notes: Board mode is already circle-pack-ish by group; this keys on spawn lineage instead. Modest novelty.
hypothesis: Keying the pack on spawn lineage (not group) shows delegation containment the current Board mode does not.
falsifier: If parent->child links are unresolvable, or the result is visually indistinguishable from the existing Board's group packing, it adds nothing.
witness: GET /api/sessions → confirm resolvable parent links exist AND differ from the group hierarchy Board uses; needs both to justify a new mode.

name: Token/Cost Waffle by Agent
what_it_shows: Proportional unit-square grid of token spend attributed to each agent.
notes: Cheap, friendly proportion glyph for the Overview tab. Pure rect grid.
hypothesis: Token spend is unevenly split across agents, which a waffle communicates more intuitively than a number.
falsifier: If one agent accounts for ~100% of tokens, the waffle is a single-color block conveying nothing a label wouldn't.
witness: GET /api/sessions → sum total_output_tokens+total_input_tokens grouped by origin_agent; needs the top agent to be <~90% of the total for the split to read.

name: Per-Project Horizon Chart
what_it_shows: Compact folded-area bands of activity for many projects stacked in little space.
notes: Dense small-multiples of activity; good when there are many projects. Hand-rolled banding over area.
hypothesis: There are enough projects with time-varying activity that dense folded-area small-multiples beat a single stacked chart.
falsifier: If only a couple of projects are active, plain area charts are clearer and horizon banding is gratuitous complexity.
witness: GET /api/sessions → count projects with activity on ≥ ~5 distinct days; needs ≥ ~8 such projects for horizon's density payoff.

name: Session Similarity Voronoi
what_it_shows: Sessions positioned by a 2D projection with Voronoi cells for easy hit-testing and neighborhood reading.
notes: Needs a projection step (PCA/UMAP offline) to be meaningful; high cost, speculative payoff.
hypothesis: A 2D projection of session features forms interpretable neighborhoods (clusters of similar sessions) worth partitioning into cells.
falsifier: If the projection yields no discernible clustering (points uniformly scattered), the Voronoi partition is arbitrary and meaningless.
witness: Offline: project session feature vectors (events/tokens/duration) to 2D and test for cluster structure (e.g. silhouette > ~0.2); needs real clustering before building.
